TAKEHOME-LOG.md

Take-home working log (append-only)

Purpose: keep a dated trail of reasoning and receipts while you do the assignment, so provenance is real-time, not reconstructed. Rule: add entries; never edit past ones. Corrections go in a new entry that says what changed and why. Git history is the second timestamp: commit this file as you go.

Rules

  1. Log before you act on any material choice, then record the result after.
  2. AI use is disclosed here (monday's interview policy): what tool, what for, what you changed or rejected. Be able to explain every line.
  3. One-way doors (hard to reverse) get a write-lock entry first: what, why, alternatives, who decides.
  4. Sources: every factual claim or number cites where it came from.
  5. No retroactive rationale: if you decided something by feel, say so.

Entry template

### YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM · short title
- Context: what I am trying to do and the constraint
- Options considered: A / B / C
- Choice and why: 
- Evidence or source: 
- Assumptions (to test): 
- AI used: tool, purpose, what I accepted or rejected
- One-way door? yes / no (if yes: write-lock)
- Result / follow-up (added later, dated):

Behavioral: five stories (situation, your call, result)

Skills-based

Scenario

  • Week 6, executive sponsor sees no adoption: meet the sponsor first, show usage by role, name the gating step, fix the workflow before adding features, and reset the success measure honestly.
  • Customer asks for something the platform cannot do: clarify the underlying outcome, offer a workaround, and file it to product with evidence from the account.
  • An agent errs in production: contain it, find the root cause, add the case to the eval set, tell the customer plainly, and report it to product.
  • Two strategic accounts need you at once: protect the committed outcome dates, communicate early, and bring in help rather than quietly dropping one.

Take-home or case-study method

Restate the goal and the success measure, list assumptions and constraints, give a three-step plan, name the top risks, say what you would measure, and time-box it. The team walkthrough tests your reasoning, so you must be able to explain every choice. Their AI policy means disclose any AI use and be able to defend all of it.

14. Tell me about yourself, v2 (adds monday at Squat, caps at about 90 seconds)

"I'm a product and technology builder who embeds with customers and owns the outcome, not just the build. The thread through my career is going inside someone else's organization to make something hard actually ship. At Squat I was the sole product and technology partner on a seven-figure engagement inside a $350M-ARR company, and I owned monday.com there as the team's work platform, so I've been your customer. At Twill Health I tested three AI-enabled product lines and recommended stopping on one. At Grayscale I ran product for ten regulated digital-asset products, about seven billion in assets, and cut release-cycle time 35 percent across four time zones with no violations. Since 2025 I've been building ARCS, an agentic platform on Claude with an MCP server and evals. The lesson: an agent's report of success isn't evidence. That's why this role caught my eye: your thesis is that enterprises struggle to deploy AI, not access it, and I can zoom out to the executive decision and zoom in to the build. What would you like to dig into?" Lead with the result in the first 20 seconds. Do not offer a demo.

15. How the Sam call ran (Oct 7) and what it means for the 30 minutes

  • Order she used: background overview → why leave founder mode → coding languages → business outcome you owned (Ideal Protein) → changed an executive decision (WTA) → hybrid → start date → your questions → comp, visa.
  • What went wrong: your opener ran several minutes and you began offering a demo. She redirected and said she is not very technical.
  • What landed: the 40 percent qualified-leads number once she asked for it, and the WTA phased-rollout story. She liked that you can zoom out and in.
  • Implications: cap the opener at 90 seconds; answer with the result first; expect Stefan to repeat the business-outcome and executive-influence prompts, probably deeper because he may have Sam's notes. See the cue card page 3 for the minute-by-minute plan.

Three habits for consistency in a recorded call

  1. Say the same number the same way every time, in the same units.
  2. When you do not remember, say "my figure" or "roughly," never a new number.
  3. If a document and your memory disagree, trust the published document and say "as the case study puts it."

monday.com take-home prep: what monday publishes, how good its evals are, and where ARCS fits

Scope and limits: this is built only from the supplied static crawl (2026-10-08), three skeptic passes, and the specialist lenses. Nothing was cloned, installed or run, and I did not re-open primary sources. "Verified" means a reader saw it in source or docs. It does not mean anyone executed it. "Inferred" means reasoned from verified facts. The crawl's developer-docs section and the architect lens were cut off mid-sentence in the input, and so was the last skeptic block. Any corrections in the lost text are not reflected here. The take-home prompt itself was not in the inputs.

Developer docs.

  • Machine-readable: .md suffix on pages, plus /api-reference/llms.txt and /apps/llms.txt. Verified.
  • MCP calls consume the API budget: MCP calls run as GraphQL, so they count against the daily limit (1,000 on Free/Standard/Basic, 10,000 on Pro, 25,000 on Enterprise). Per-minute limits are 1,000, 2,500 and 5,000. Concurrency limits are 40, 100 and 250. Verified. (rate-limits.md)
  • MCP security page: It says MCP actions run under the user's own permissions. It assigns prompt-injection and output validation to the customer or AI client. It says self-service export of detailed MCP or API audit logs is not available. Verified. (monday-mcp-security-overview.md)
  • Models API: An OpenAI-compatible gateway at api.monday.com/platform-ai-gateway/openai/v1. Upstreams are OpenAI and Anthropic only. Billing is in "monday AI tokens", with a per-call x-monday-credits-used header. No numeric rates or gateway rate limits were found. Verified. (changelog/consume-ai-models-through-monday; getting-started-with-the-models-api.md)
  • Bring-your-own model: Unsupported, per search summaries of monday's FAQ that nobody read directly. Inferred.

2) Verdict on Sensei and the other off-the-shelf evals

Sensei (mondaycom/sensei) is a demo-grade smoke harness, not a qualification standard.

Why it should not be treated as monday's standard:

  • Created 2026-03-15, last push 2026-03-22, v0.0.3, 20 stars, 7 issues and PRs ever.
  • Commits trace to AgentTalent.ai and "Nymeria", with early multi-agent AI build messages.
  • SECURITY.md routes reports to a personal Gmail address.
  • monday's docs index never mentions it.
  • Verified for the facts above; the "AI-built and adopted" reading is inferred. (gh api repos/mondaycom/sensei; SECURITY.md; developer.monday.com/api-reference/llms.txt)

What it does well (verified):

  • Clean YAML suite schema, with Zod (a schema validation library) checking suites at load.
  • Transparent scoring math: KPI to scenario to layer, weighted 50/30/20, with badge cutoffs at 90, 75 and 60.
  • Deterministic KPI primitives: contains, regex, json-schema, json-parse, numeric-range, word-count.
  • Seeded scenario pools.
  • A multi_judge option (several judge calls, median score) reachable from suite YAML.
  • An HTML report and duration_ms timings.
  • (packages/engine/src/{scorer,types,schema,loader}.ts)

Where it fails as an eval (verified by reading source, not executed):

  • The judge never sees the fixtures. It gets only the prompt string, so accuracy KPIs such as personalization are scored on plausibility. A fluent fabrication scores like a grounded answer. (runner.ts runScenario; cli/src/commands/run.ts; judge.ts inputContext)
  • Fixtures are also dropped on two of the four agent adapters. The openai-compat and langserve adapters forward only previous_output and feedback. Only http and stdio forward the full context. A hosted-model or Ollama run through openai-compat scores two models inventing a prospect. (adapters/openai-compat.ts 107-120; adapters/langserve.ts 88-94; adapters/http.ts 67; adapters/stdio.ts 145)
  • The agent's model name cannot be set from YAML or the CLI. AgentConfig has no model field, so it is always 'default'. That blocks same-gateway model comparisons through the CLI. The key-stripping step is standard Zod behavior and was not run. (openai-compat.ts line 58; types.ts; schema.ts)
  • Judge controls are minimal:
  • Single model, default gpt-4o, temperature 0.
  • No order randomization, length control or cross-family judge.
  • The judge's confidence value is collected and never used.
  • parseVerdict rejects only NaN, with no clamp.
  • A judge outage becomes a KPI score of 0 instead of a failed run.
  • (judge.ts; runner.ts catch block)
  • multi_judge is not a bias fix. It makes three calls to the same model at temperature 0 and takes the median. The rate_limit and retry YAML keys are stripped by the schema (inferred, standard Zod behavior).
  • Layers 2 and 3 are weak.
  • The "interview" is a fresh prompt with the previous output prepended.
  • "Self-improvement" appends a static feedback string.
  • The comparator never interpolates the per-KPI rubric, has no order blinding and has no timeout.
  • (runner.ts; comparator.ts)
  • Reproducibility fields are partly missing. Results carry agent_id, timestamp, judge_model, transcripts and durations. They lack run id, seed, judge-prompt version and cost. (types.ts)
  • scenarios_per_layer is dead. pickScenariosByLayer is called nowhere in the runner or CLI. The shipped suites use no pools and no multi_judge.
  • Suite coverage is thin:
  • Suites are SDR (sales development rep), support, content, and three novelty suites.
  • Only SDR has fixtures.
  • The README's QA, Data Analysis and Developer suites do not exist.
  • (suites/*/suite.yaml)
  • Safety surface: a downloaded marketplace suite can set agent.command for the stdio adapter and spawn processes. No suite signing was seen (inferred). (adapters/stdio.ts; registry-client.ts)

Two corrections to claims in the specialist lenses:

  • "Only automated check is word-count" is true of shipped suites but misleading. The engine has six deterministic primitives. What is missing is labeled data wired to them. The function KPI type returns 0 on the CLI path. Some SDR rubrics also name expected facts, which gives the judge a weak coverage check. (scorer.ts 38-170; suites/sdr-qualification/suite.yaml 51-125)
  • "A catastrophic layer failure can still earn silver or gold" overstates it. By my arithmetic from the 50/30/20 weights, a zero in a full three-layer suite caps the overall score as follows. This is inferred from LAYER_WEIGHTS and BADGE_THRESHOLDS.
Layer scored zeroBest possible overallBadge
Reasoning70bronze
Self-improvement80silver
Execution50no badge

The real averaging risk is inside a layer (one bad scenario among 1-3) and in layers that are absent, which renormalize. Per-KPI hard-fail gates are still missing.

Other evals:

  • agentic-monday routing eval: a 13-case smoke test of which skill fires, not task outcome.
  • 13/13 on 13 cases means the true pass rate could plausibly sit near 75% (my reading of the data scientist's exact interval: 0.025^(1/13) is about 0.75, a two-sided 95% bound).
  • The authors wrote the prompts, it ran once on one model, and the pipeline is not public.
  • mcp Jest suite: tests each tool contract against mocks. It cannot see cross-model or live-account failures such as #501, #496 and #508.
  • ATP tests: real LLM-in-the-loop approval, resume and security tests run against local Ollama models (qwen2.5-coder:7b or gpt-oss:20b). They are not in CI: test.yml runs unit and one OpenTelemetry integration test only, and lint is || true. (agent-tool-protocol/.github/workflows/test.yml; __tests__/e2e/test-config.ts)

A server-side-stateful agent can leak state across Sensei scenarios (the adapter sends a stable user key per run, with 5 scenarios in parallel).

Shape 3 corrections: the platform is better than "no controls".

  • Own OAuth app route: an org can cap scopes (for example boards:read), restrict users and client, and rotate the secret to revoke everyone. The docs say you get your own audit trail of authorized users and activity.
  • Dynamic connectors: these are early access. Tokens can keep working up to 24 hours after revocation, and admins get no email about requests.
  • Undo and annotations: undo_action and get_board_activity exist, but undo uses the unstable dev API version. Tools carry readOnlyHint and destructiveHint annotations.
  • What still holds: no self-service per-tool-call audit export, and no untrusted-content tagging.
  • Unverified: "no per-board scope" is an absence nobody confirmed either way.
  • Evidence: control-mcp-access-with-oauth-app.md; mcp-dynamic-connectors.md; undo-action-tool.ts.

4) Divergent expert perspectives

  • Data scientist (validity): The scores have no demonstrated meaning. The sample is tiny (n of 1-3 per layer), there is no variance, the judge is unvalidated and the KPIs are mostly opinion. Fix first: ground-truth KPIs, then calibration.
  • ML engineer (operations): The practical blockers are determinism, silent-zero failures, missing cost and run metadata, and weak local-model support. Advice: lead with the smallest fix for an observed flaw, not a rebuild.
  • RL and agents researcher (trajectory): Text-in/text-out cannot score tool use, credit assignment, long-horizon recovery, or whether "self-improvement" is real. Proposes counterfactual replay, learning curves with held-out sibling tasks, fault-injected sandbox episodes, and indirect-injection scenarios scored on obedience.
  • Systems architect (deployment): The larger risks sit on the platform side, not in Sensei:
  • no per-call audit export;
  • unsanitized returned data next to write tools, which is the "lethal trifecta" shape (untrusted content, private data, write or exfiltration ability);
  • read-only being a registration filter;
  • apps mode able to promote an app;
  • failed writes returned as success (#501) next to a daily call cap.
  • The fixes are customer-side: gateway audit sink, low-privilege service users, read-after-write checks, dedupe ledger, quota allocator.

Disagreements and how they resolve:

  1. Is multi_judge reachable? The RL lens and the crawl said no. The skeptic showed it is reachable through YAML and simply unused. It is still not a bias control.
  2. Do the badges launder catastrophic failure? The data scientist and RL lenses said yes. The arithmetic above says only partly: a reasoning zero caps at bronze, a self-improvement zero still earns silver.
  3. Scope. The ML engineer says start small, while the RL lens lists nine proposals. Treat the RL list as a menu, not a plan. The sequencing in section 5 follows the ML engineer.
  4. Local models. The architect and ML engineer said "partial". The skeptic found fixture-dropping, the fixed model name, the key requirement and fully mocked tests, and downgraded to gap.
  5. Wasted JSON-parse retries at temperature 0 are the ML engineer's inference. Nobody tested them.
  6. Sensei's status. The architect rated it "partial". The skeptic's provenance evidence points to "unadopted side project".

5) ARCS plug plan with honest status

These ARCS claims come from the plug input and the repo's own docs. I did not re-verify them. None has been run against a monday agent, and everything below is a proposal until built. ARCS is the user's own decision-intelligence system. Its Y-gate is a state check that can force a RED result. Its Kintsugi rule means a failure is shown, never silently patched. WRITE-LOCK means a one-way action requires an explicit declaration first.

Recommended order (my sequencing, following the ML engineer's advice):

  1. Fix fixture pass-through, clamping and fail-on-judge-error.
  2. Add the per-run receipt: run id, seed, judge-prompt hash, model and cost.
  3. Wire labeled ground-truth checks.
  4. Add trace capture and the board-state diff.
  5. Add hard-fail gates.
  6. Add trials and intervals.

6) Risks and what NOT to claim

Do not claim:

  • That Sensei is monday's evaluation standard, adopted, or maintained. It is dormant with no commits after 2026-03-22.
  • That the tool count is exactly 90, or that the README tool list is current. 90 is a floor from a regex.
  • That monday's hosted MCP server enforces or lacks any control. Its source is not public.
  • That monday has no audit at all. Say instead that there is no self-service per-tool-call export. Security-event audit logs exist, and the OAuth route offers some tracking.
  • That monday has a Hugging Face presence, or that its hosted AI supports open weights or bring-your-own models.
  • That ARCS calibration is proven. Outcome capture is low, so present it as a discipline.
  • That any code, test or eval was run. This is a static read, and counts are grep-based.
  • That ATP is part of monday's official MCP stack, or that its injection defense is on by default. Provenance defaults to off and no injection benchmark is published.
  • That the 13/13 skill-routing result shows task quality.

Interview-day risks:

  • Presenting a gap list as criticism of named maintainers. Frame it as "what an eval needs next", not "what is broken".
  • Overscoping. A take-home rewards one flaw found, reproduced and fixed, not the nine-item menu.
  • Counts and issue states drift daily. Re-pull them before quoting.
  • Confidence in the sources:
  • Verified items were read by one reader, and some skeptic claims also rest on a single read.
  • Search-summary claims about monday AI data retention and the FAQ are second-hand. Do not repeat them as fact.

7) What to read or test first

Read, in this order (about 90 minutes):

  1. monday-mcp-security-overview.md, then control-mcp-access-with-oauth-app.md. These set what the customer owns.
  2. mondaycom/mcp issues #501, #496 and #508, plus tools-filtering.utils.ts and undo-action-tool.ts. These are the concrete failure modes.
  3. Sensei's runner.ts, judge.ts, cli/src/commands/run.ts, adapters/openai-compat.ts and scorer.ts. These contain every verified defect above.
  4. rate-limits.md and getting-started-with-the-models-api.md, for the cost and quota facts.

Test first (each is a falsification of a claim that was only read, not run; about 2 hours):

  1. Run one Sensei suite with the judge prompt logged. Confirm the fixtures are absent from it.
  2. Point it at an openai-compat stub and confirm the fixtures never reach the agent. Then try http.
  3. Return a judge score of 15 on a 10-point scale and a malformed JSON reply. Confirm there is no clamp and that the KPI becomes 0.
  4. Try a model: key in agent YAML and see whether it is stripped.
  5. Set multi_judge: true in YAML and confirm it takes effect, so you do not repeat the "unreachable" error.
  6. If the take-home arrives as a repo or archive from a recruiter, scan it with the sbom-payload-scan skill before opening or installing anything.

Anything that fails to reproduce should be struck from the story before it is told.

research/monday-oss-forensics-critic.md

Completeness critique

1. Modalities and sources not run or read

  • Nothing executed. No clone, no Sensei run, no stub adapter, no sandbox monday account, no hosted-MCP call. The report's core defects are source reads only, and it lists them as "test first" itself.
  • The take-home prompt is absent. The ranking, the "fix one flaw" advice and the 6-step order are all ungrounded. If the take-home is built on Sensei or on another eval, the plan may be irrelevant.
  • Three truncations. Developer docs, the architect lens and the last skeptic block were cut off. Lost corrections may contradict current text, yet the report uses verdict language.
  • "Their dev documentation" is ambiguous. The request could mean GitHub and Hugging Face documentation. Nothing from HF docs or eval tooling (lighteval, smolagents, TRL, Inspect) was read. Nothing covered third-party MCP and agent benchmarks that include monday tasks. HF was only checked for a monday org.
  • Sources unread:
  • monday engineering blog, product pages, changelog for Sidekick, Agent Factory and vibe

2. Claims unverified or in tension

  • "Verified" is defined as "a reader saw it in source", and the report mixes it with unrun inferences. Fixture dropping, the fixed 'default' model and the missing judge clamp are labeled verified. The Zod key-stripping behind the model key and the rate_limit/retry keys is admitted unrun. Shape 5 is rated "Gap" while the text says the config path is "plausible but untested".
  • Tool count arithmetic: 33 + 54 + 2 = 89, but the text says "at least about 90".
  • Badge math: the layer-to-weight mapping is never stated. The 70/80/50 caps only work if execution = 50, reasoning = 30 and self-improvement = 20. Verify LAYER_WEIGHTS.
  • "Harness not published" rests on 404s for PR 729 and the run. A 404 in public API calls is also consistent with a private repo, so "unpublished" is not shown.
  • ATP ownership is unclear. It sits in the "GitHub (org mondaycom)" table, but section 6 says it is not part of the official stack. Settle which org owns it before saying either.
  • "Nine-item menu" for the RL lens: only four proposals are shown.

  • "Dormant, no commits after 2026-03-22" is a crawl snapshot. Branches, forks and other repos were not checked.
  • "monday's docs index never mentions it" is absence from llms.txt only.

  • ARCS claims are unverified:
  • existence and behavior of provenance_lint.py, receipt_outcome_resolver.py and arcs-verb-eval
  • the Drift Sentinel

3. Over-confident language

  • "Demo-grade", "not a qualification standard", "unadopted side project" and "AI-built" rest on repo metadata and commit messages.
  • The gap ratings rest on absence from public GitHub, but monday's internal evals are invisible to a crawl. They should read "no public evidence of", not "Gap".
  • "No HF presence" rests on a code search the report admits can miss things.
  • "Fixtures never reach the judge/agent" is an unrun inference.
  • The architect's risks mix local-server behavior (registration-filter read-only, apps mode) with the hosted server, whose source is unseen.

4. Could embarrass the candidate in front of a monday hiring manager

  • Biggest risk: Sensei is a mondaycom repo. The HM, the team or the take-home author may have written it or may care about it. Calling it "AI-built", naming AgentTalent.ai and Nymeria, and noting the personal-Gmail SECURITY.md is petty. If any of it is wrong, it costs credibility. Drop the named third parties and the Gmail point. Frame it as "what an eval needs next".
  • ATP's hard-coded JWT secret and the ATP security claims could land on someone's own project.
  • ARCS jargon (Y-gate, Kintsugi, WRITE-LOCK, Golden Inchworm) is private vocabulary. A heavy ARCS plug can read as a pivot to self-promotion. The candidate's own "2 of 247" capture rate undercuts the calibration pitch if raised.
  • Unrun defect claims stated as fact, if one fails to reproduce in front of the HM.
  • Drifting counts (stars, versions, issue states, tool count) stated from a stale snapshot.

Process gatekeeper: Recruiter. Dealbreaker: a policy breach (undisclosed AI use, forwarding the link, wrong packaging). Path: disqualification before anyone reads it. Control: the rubric's hard gates H1 to H12.

Round-robin protocol: the Greek chorus as two passes and a reconcile

  • Strophe (top-down pass): read the draft from Executive to Surgical. Does the story stay coherent as detail increases, and does each level get what it needs?
  • Antistrophe (bottom-up pass): read from Surgical to Executive. Is every higher-level claim supported by evidence one level down? Build a claim ladder: each executive claim, the strategic argument beneath it, the operational plan, the tactical steps, and the surgical evidence.
  • Epode (reconcile): list conflicts (executives want brevity, surgical readers want depth), resolve them by layering and linking, and book each change as a kintsugi seam.
  • Per voice: objection, response with evidence, change to the deliverable.
  • Order of depth for first, second, third order: for each dealbreaker, test the first-order consequence, then ask what that causes next, then what it causes after that. If the third-order consequence is severe, fix the first-order cause now.
  • Stop after two full rounds. Log every change.

Design for fast consensus (inside their process)

  • One spine, ten entry points. A one-page executive summary leads: outcome, approach, proof, rollout, risks, next step. Then short role-labeled sections ("If you care about architecture, read here") so each voice finds its answer fast.
  • Show, don't tell: link proof the reader can open in seconds.
  • No surprises: state assumptions, limits and what you did not do.
  • Same numbers everywhere: one source per claim.
  • Respect the 10 MB and two-folder format; put the spine in presentation/ and the build in source/.

Anticipatory objections to your candidacy (answer ahead)

  1. "Is the engineering depth enough?" About a year and a half of daily TypeScript, all on ARCS; the take-home is the proof.
  2. "Is this a founder who will leave?" Applying for a full-time role; ARCS is how you learn the technology.
  3. "Is the governance talk real?" Show the practice: evidence rules, audit trail, change control, in your own words from Grayscale and Squat.
  4. "Is AI doing the work?" The log: every AI use disclosed, every choice explainable, rejected alternatives recorded.
  5. "Will it generalize?" The reusable-pattern section.

Next

After you read the brief: write the outline, run round 1, build, run round 2, then package. I can run the rounds with separate agents per voice; it costs several hundred thousand tokens, so I'd run it only on a real draft.

  4. Quality measured at full coverage, with a stated pass bar.
  5. Governance proportionate to the scenario (evidence, PII, audit, change control).
  6. AI-assisted building shown plainly, with your reasoning and rejected alternatives logged.

Altitude and friction audit method

ALTITUDE-FRICTION-AUDIT-method.md

Altitude and friction audit: a reusable discovery method

Use it when the problem space is new or undefined, and you need to plan, prioritize and find friction without trusting one point of view. Source: the chorus gauntlet built for the monday.com take-home, generalized. Contains no personal data. In a real organization, replace hypothesized personas with interviews.

Core idea

Every initiative is read at five altitudes by people with different decisions and dealbreakers. Friction shows up where the same initiative looks different at different altitudes, or where detail gets lost between them. Tracing consequences three orders deep tells you which friction to fix first.

Steps

  1. Map stakeholders by altitude. Executive, strategic, operational, tactical, surgical. Add department. Mark who decides, who influences, who reviews, and who can veto on process or policy.
  2. For each altitude, record: the decision they own, their read budget (how long they will give it), and the fidelity that satisfies them.
  3. Elicit dealbreakers. Ask each persona (or real person): "What would make you say no? What would make you not look further?" Record the exact words.
  4. Trace three orders. For each dealbreaker: first order (what happens directly), second order (what that causes), third order (what that causes after). Fix the first-order cause when the third-order result is severe.
  5. Build the claim ladder. Each top-level claim, then the argument under it, then the plan, then the steps, then the evidence. Mark any rung with no support.
  6. Find friction hotspots: conflicts between altitudes (executives want brevity, surgical readers want depth), handoffs that lose detail, claims that change between levels, and numbers that disagree.
  7. Find the consonance spine: what many altitudes want first. Lead with it.
  8. Prioritize each friction item on: severity at the third order, how many altitudes it touches, reversibility (is it a one-way door?), cost to fix, and strength of evidence.
  9. Design cheap tests. For each top item, state a falsifier: what observation would show you are wrong.
  10. Log decisions with dates and sources so the trail is real-time, not reconstructed.

Discovery questions by altitude

AltitudeAsk
ExecutiveWhat outcome would make this worth your attention? What would make you stop it? What number do you watch?
StrategicWhat does this need to be consistent with? What are you sequencing it against? What has to be true for it to scale?
OperationalWhat does running this cost in time and people? Where do handoffs break? What do you need to estimate and staff it?
TacticalWhat does a user do first? Where do people get stuck? What would you need to teach it?
SurgicalWhat could be wrong or unsafe? Which edge cases matter? How would we know it is working?

For an undefined problem space, add

  • Quiet signals: what people avoid saying, what they route around, what they check twice.
  • Abductive prompts: "What is the best explanation for this friction?" Then state a test that would kill the explanation.
  • Inliers and false positives: list friction that looks real but is explained by something simpler, and test it before acting.
  • One-way doors: flag decisions that are hard to reverse and require an explicit sign-off first.

Outputs

A stakeholder-by-altitude map, a ranked friction list with three-order paths, a consonance spine, a short list of cheap tests, and a dated decision log.

Where it is useful

Organizational planning and prioritization, a friction audit of a process or rollout, a discovery phase for a customer deployment, and the take-home's discovery section.

Hardened rubric and gates

TAKEHOME-RUBRIC-hardened.md

Hardened grading rubric v0: monday.com take-home

Private. Built from: the invitation checklist (known), the pre-mortem failure modes (FM1 to FM13), monday's AI interview policy, the JD, and sensei's style of KPIs. Reconcile after you read the real pre-read, video and checklist: add or change rows, and mark each row's source (invitation, pre-read, JD, self). Until then every score is provisional.

Protocol (dual bar raiser, as defined in .claude/arcs-dual-bar-raiser.md)

  • Implementer (you, with Claude Code) drafts and edits. The Implementer never self-clears.
  • Bar-Raiser is an independent reviewer (a fresh-context agent that has not seen your reasoning, a different model, or a human). It issues a verdict: CLEAR, CONDITIONAL CLEAR with annotated findings, or HOLD.
  • Annotation taxonomy (from the protocol): IMPL_GAP (a requirement not met), CONSISTENCY (a claim disagrees with another claim), COLLISION (disagrees with a public page, resume or the brief), STYLE.
  • Kintsugi: every break found after the first draft is booked in TAKEHOME-LOG.md as break, how found, repair, guard, before the fix. No silent patching.
  • Two audience bars both must clear: Bar A (customer outcome) and Bar B (builder defense). A third, the KILL bar, covers hard gates.
  • Deterministic gates and scored judgment stay separate: a gate fail is a kill, never averaged away.

Hard gates (any fail = KILL; fix or cut, never average)

2Scoping and assumptionshidden assumptionsassumptions stated, ambiguity questions asked, a not-doing listA

Bar clears when every dimension on that bar scores at least 2 and the bar's average is at least 2.3. Both A and B must clear.

Pathogen detection (run on the final draft)

  • Temporal paradox: dates and sequence claims (when built, when decided) agree with git history, the log and the public pages.
  • Speaker provenance: who said or decided what is stated correctly (what monday said versus what you inferred).
  • Unsupported numbers and "every/always/never" statements.
  • Production, public, compliant, certified: each word is checked against evidence.
  • Collision with: the resume lines, the Ideal Protein case study, status.arcs.care, good.arcs.care, and the consistency sheet.

Red team and blue team (bounded)

  1. Round 1: a fresh agent receives only the brief, the rubric and the deliverable, and is told to refute and default to HOLD.
  2. Blue: you fix, logging each seam first.
  3. Round 2 only if round 1 returned a HOLD or a kill finding. Then stop. No open-ended polishing.
  4. If a section still fails a gate and time is short: cut it rather than patch it.

Mechanical gates to run (deterministic)

provenance_lint with a ledger; slop_lint; em-dash grep; package.sh; link check (HTTP 200) for every external URL; a secrets grep over source/ and presentation/; consistency check against STORY-CONSISTENCY-CHECK.md.

Timeline (7 days)

Day 1: activate, watch the video, read the pre-read, reconcile this rubric, write acceptance criteria. Days 2 to 4: build in thin slices, log as you go. Day 5: draft the deck, mechanical gates. Day 6: red and blue round, rehearse the walkthrough aloud. Day 7 (Oct 14): final gates, package, submit the evening before the deadline.

Simulation-informed priorities (Monte Carlo pre-mortem, Oct 8)

Model and priors: takehome-workspace/montecarlo_premortem.py (stdlib, seeded, 40,000 runs per estimate). The priors are my subjective estimates, not data; these figures expose assumptions and rank pre-work, they do not predict outcomes. Rerun after you read the brief with updated priors.

  • Passing all bars with no pre-work: about 0.24. The KILL bar (process, pathogen, hardening, kintsugi) drives about 0.37 of failures and is the cheapest to fix.
  • Best value per hour: log every repair first (0.5 h), the confidentiality rule (0.5 h), a one-time-link dry run (1.5 h), claim and consistency gates (2 h).
  • Next: outcome-first framing (2 h) and acceptance criteria with a not-doing list (3 h), then rehearse the walkthrough (4 h).
  • Red team: the weakest points are monday platform fluency and "engineering demo, not outcome"; the worst pair is those two together.
  • With about 15.5 h of pre-work the model estimates about 0.52; reading the brief, rehearsing aloud, a packaging dry run, passing the gates, and an independent bar-raiser clear take it to about 0.65. Pre-work alone does not reach 0.65, so the evidence steps matter.

ZIP packaging check (script)

takehome-workspace/package.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Package the monday.com take-home: ONE zip under 10 MB with non-empty source/ and presentation/.
# Usage: ./package.sh   (run from takehome-workspace). Builds ../submission.zip and verifies it. Never uploads anything.
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"; cd "$HERE"
OUT="$HERE/submission.zip"; LIMIT=$((10*1024*1024))
for d in source presentation; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && [ -n "$(find "$d" -type f ! -name '.DS_Store' | head -1)" ] || { echo "FAIL: $d/ is missing or empty"; exit 1; }
done
rm -f "$OUT"
zip -qr "$OUT" source presentation -x '*/.DS_Store' '*/node_modules/*' '*/.git/*' '*/.env*' '*/*.key' '*/*.pem'
SIZE=$(stat -f%z "$OUT" 2>/dev/null || stat -c%s "$OUT")
echo "zip: $OUT  size: $SIZE bytes (limit $LIMIT)"
[ "$SIZE" -lt "$LIMIT" ] || { echo "FAIL: zip is 10 MB or larger"; exit 1; }
echo "contents:"; unzip -l "$OUT" | sed -n '4,$p' | head -40
if unzip -l "$OUT" | grep -q -i -E '\.env|secret|token|password|\.pem|\.key'; then echo "WARN: a secret-looking filename is inside the zip"; fi
echo "OK: structure and size pass. Now complete every checklist item in the portal before submitting."

Blind pre-mortem (17 failure modes)

PREMORTEM-takehome-blind.md

Blind pre-mortem: monday.com take-home (written before opening the link)

Private. "Blind" means: written without seeing the assignment, from the role, the call, public research and patterns at other companies. Update after the forensic research lands and again after you read the assignment.

Frame: it is two weeks from now and you did not advance. Why? Ranked by likelihood times damage.

Quiet signals to design for

  • They may weigh how you handle ambiguity and communication as much as the output.
  • Engineer peers will read the build; the hiring manager will read the narrative. Serve both in one document.
  • A reviewer who sees "worked fast with AI, cannot explain it" will mark it down faster than a modest but fully owned result.

Right level of pre-work (do this, not that)

  • Do: scaffolding: the log, a deliverable skeleton, an evidence ledger, a rehearsal plan, a sandbox for monday fluency, and your clarifying questions.
  • Do not: pre-solve a problem you have not seen, or pre-build the answer. If the brief forbids prior work or AI, you need to know first.

Questions to ask Sam before you open the link

  1. Is there a time limit once the link is opened, and what happens if the browser session is lost?
  2. What is the expected time commitment, deadline and submission format (deck, doc, video, working build)?
  3. Is AI allowed for the assignment, and what disclosure do they want?
  4. Who is the audience for the review, and what are they scoring?
  5. Will I work in a trial account, and what tools or models may I use?
  6. How is take-home work stored and who owns it afterward?

Go / no-go to open the link

  • [ ] Question answers received, or the unknowns accepted
  • [ ] A protected block of time and a stable connection
  • [ ] Log started and the AI-use rule written
  • [ ] Sandbox practice done; deliverable skeleton ready
  • [ ] Confidentiality rule understood
  • [ ] A time cap decided, with a plan to submit at the cap

To add after the forensic research

Findings from monday's open-source repos and docs (what sensei really does, MCP details, local-model support) will become additional checks here.

Update: mechanics from the invitation (Oct 8)

  • The deadline is fixed: Thursday Oct 15, 5pm ET. The session stays open until submission, revocation or the deadline, so activation does not start a personal timer. That argues for activating soon, to see the real brief and still have days to ask questions.
  • One-time link (credential): activate once, in the browser and device you will finish on, with the exact invited email. Bookmark the dashboard. No incognito, no clearing cookies, no switching browsers, no forwarding. Decide the browser now and check that no extension clears cookies.
  • Deliverable: one ZIP under 10 MB with non-empty source/ and presentation/ folders. That limit rules out a large video; plan a compact deck or a small recording. A packaging and size-check script is ready at takehome-workspace/package.sh.
  • Required steps: watch the whole intro video, review the pre-read and materials, complete every checklist item. Budget time for these before building.
  • Still unknown (behind the link): the problem itself, the AI policy for the assignment, and the scoring.

Update from the forensic research (Oct 8)

Read-only static research on monday's GitHub, Hugging Face and developer docs is in research/monday-oss-forensics-report.md, with a completeness critic. New failure modes:

  • FM14 (High damage): criticizing monday's own repo. Sensei is a mondaycom repo; the hiring manager or the take-home author may care about it. Frame gaps as "what an eval needs next," never "what is broken," and do not name third parties.
  • FM15 (High damage): stating unrun findings as fact. The defect claims were read in source, not executed. Reproduce them or label them. A claim that fails to reproduce in front of a reviewer costs more than not making it.
  • FM16 (Medium): stale counts. Stars, versions, issue states and tool counts drift daily. Re-pull before quoting.
  • FM17 (Medium): heavy ARCS vocabulary or a pivot to self-promotion. Your own outcome-capture numbers undercut a calibration pitch if raised. Present ARCS as a discipline, not a proof.
  • Responsible disclosure: the research flagged a default JWT secret in a protocol repo. If it is real, treat it as a private maintainer matter, not interview material.

Rubric gates H11 and H12 now cover these.

Kairos and compounding

KAIROS-COMPOUNDING-layer.md

Kairos and compounding layer (private; added to the chorus)

Adds the "time signature" questions every voice is asking underneath their objections, and defines what to build so value compounds. Run it after the epode as a final pass on the outline and the draft.

The five time-signature questions (every persona asks these, in their own words)

  1. Why now (kairos)? What about this moment makes this the right time?
  2. Why this instrument? Why are you the right tool for this job?
  3. Can you actually play it? Where is the proof of mastery across the instruments the job needs?
  4. Does this make my life easier? Less time, less energy, less frustration, more trust and clarity.
  5. What will compound? What do we keep after this engagement that makes the next one faster?

Honest answers, and what to avoid

1. Why now. Evidence-based timing, from public facts only: monday relaunched as an AI work platform in May 2026; the strategic CS and FDE practice formed in February 2026; deployment-strategy roles appeared in Sept and Oct 2026. Compounding is cheapest while a practice is young. Say what you know and keep it light. Do not claim insight into internal plans.

2 and 3. Right tool, can you play the instruments. Do not claim "better than any other candidate": you cannot know the field, and the claim invites a fight you cannot win. Prove range with receipts instead. Each instrument has a proof, an honest tempo, and a limit.

InstrumentProof you can showHonest limit
Executive and outcome framingGrayscale gates and results; the outcome-first structure of the deliverableFew post-launch adoption measures in your record
Delivery and scopingSquat sole ownership; WTA phased rolloutResults for some stories not yet filled in
Integration and APIsThe take-home build; your MCP tool layer (private)About a year and a half of daily TypeScript; no customer on the MCP layer yet
Agents and evalsAI-use log; evals with a pass bar; public ARCS surfacesOutcome capture on ARCS is low; say so
Governance in regulated settingsEvidence, PII, audit, change control, one-way doors in your own wordsNot certified; a design discipline, not a compliance claim
The monday platformA tenant you set up with role-based access (about 20 users)Agents, vibe apps and MCP in a customer setting not yet done

Adaptive time signature means shifting altitude and tempo to the audience: 60 seconds for an executive, 30 minutes for a surgical reader. That is the skill Sam noticed ("zooming out and in"). Show it in how the deliverable is layered.

4. Make my life easier. Say it in each altitude's currency.

AltitudeWhat it saves them
ExecutiveDecision time and risk: one sentence, one sourced number
StrategicCoherence: a plan that fits the rest of the strategy
OperationalEstimation and staffing effort: a ready estimate, RACI and handoff
TacticalTeaching effort: steps and templates they can reuse
SurgicalVerification effort: tests, failure modes, honest limits

Across all of them: fewer surprises, shared language, and a log that shows how decisions were made (trust).

5. What compounds. Candidate assets, each reusable by the practice and across client scopes. Choose one or two after reading the brief; do not promise all.

AssetWhat it compressesHow you would measure it
Engagement playbook (scope, success measure, build, evals, change control, adoption, feedback to product)Time from kickoff to first valueDays to first value, engagement one versus engagement two
Discovery and friction-audit templateDiscovery effort and reworkHours to a ranked friction list
Connector pattern library with read-after-write checksIntegration defects and support loadDefects per integration
Agent qualification harness that fixes known gaps (fixtures reach agent and judge, run metadata, hard-fail checks)Time to trust a new agentRuns to a stable pass rate
Receipts (one decision record per engagement)Re-explaining and audit effortTime to answer "why did we do this?"
Governance pack for regulated clients (data classes, model tiers, approvals)Security review cyclesDays in review
Land-and-expand map (first value, then expansion triggers)Time from first win to the next scopeTime to second scope

Compounding without hype. Say "compress time to value," not "exponentially." Treat compounding as a hypothesis with a falsifier: if engagement two with the kit is not faster than engagement one on days to first value, the asset is not earning its place. Do not quote a percentage until you have a baseline.

Add to the chorus

  • After the epode, run the five questions against each altitude's entry point.
  • Add a "Why now, why you, what we keep" box to the one-page executive summary (three short lines).
  • In the walkthrough, show the compounding asset you chose and the single metric that will tell you if it works.

Decide after you read the brief

Which one or two assets fit the assignment, what the baseline is, and which instrument you will demonstrate live versus explain.

Monte Carlo model (script)

takehome-workspace/montecarlo_premortem.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Monte Carlo pre-mortem for the monday.com take-home. Stdlib only. Deterministic (seeded).

HONESTY: the priors below are SUBJECTIVE estimates from the blind pre-mortem, not measured data.
The output is a structured way to expose assumptions and rank pre-work, NOT a prediction.
Edit the table, rerun, and compare. Nothing here touches the real assignment.

Model
- Anterior (prior): each failure mode (FM) has a probability of occurring, scaled by latent factors
  (time pressure T, brief difficulty B) and a rejection-given-occurrence probability scaled by
  reviewer strictness S.
- Posterior: evidence events (brief read, rehearsal done, dry run, gates passed) multiply specific
  FM probabilities down; we report the readiness curve as evidence accumulates.
- Blue team: choose mitigations under an hours budget (greedy by marginal gain per hour, common random numbers).
- Red team: stress each FM (x1.8) and each pair to find the plan's weakest joint.
- Inverse reasoning: start from a target P(pass) and report the cheapest mitigation set that reaches it.
- Dual bar raiser: two audience bars (A customer-outcome, B builder-defense) must both clear, plus a KILL bar
  (pathogen / hardening / kintsugi failures). Pass = no kill event AND bar A AND bar B clear.
"""
import random, json, sys

L = {"High": 0.35, "Medium": 0.20, "Low": 0.08}
R = {"VeryHigh": 0.85, "High": 0.60, "Medium": 0.30}

 (1, "wrong question / sprawl", "High", "High", "A", 3.0, 0.60, ("B", "T")),

 ("E3 packaging + environment dry run passed", {6: .5, 11: .9}),
 ("E4 provenance / consistency / slop gates passed", {5: .5, 8: .6, 13: .6}),
 ("E5 independent bar-raiser CONDITIONAL CLEAR", {1: .8, 2: .8, 3: .8, 5: .7, 7: .7}),
]

def clip(x): return max(0.0, min(0.99, x))

def simulate(mitigated, mult, n, seed):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    ok = a_fail = b_fail = k_fail = 0
    for _ in range(n):
        T = rng.betavariate(2, 3); Bd = rng.betavariate(2, 2); S = rng.betavariate(2, 2)
        fa = fb = fk = False
        for (i, nm, lk, rj, bar, hrs, eff, drv) in FMS:
            p = L[lk] * mult.get(i, 1.0)
            if "T" in drv: p *= (0.6 + 0.8 * T)
            if "B" in drv: p *= (0.7 + 0.6 * Bd)
            if i in mitigated: p *= (1 - eff)
            if rng.random() < clip(p):
                if rng.random() < clip(R[rj] * (0.8 + 0.4 * S)):
                    if bar == "A": fa = True
                    elif bar == "B": fb = True
                    else: fk = True
        a_fail += fa; b_fail += fb; k_fail += fk
        ok += not (fa or fb or fk)
    return ok / n, a_fail / n, b_fail / n, k_fail / n

def greedy(budget, mult, n=12000, seed=7):
    chosen, spent, curve = set(), 0.0, []
    base = simulate(chosen, mult, n, seed)[0]
    while True:
        best = None
        for fm in FMS:
            i, hrs = fm[0], fm[5]
            if i in chosen or spent + hrs > budget: continue
            gain = simulate(chosen | {i}, mult, n, seed)[0] - base
            if best is None or gain / hrs > best[0]: best = (gain / hrs, i, gain, hrs)
        if not best or best[2] <= 0: break
        _, i, gain, hrs = best
        chosen.add(i); spent += hrs; base += gain; curve.append((i, round(gain, 4), hrs, round(base, 4)))
    return chosen, spent, curve

def main():
    N = 40000; BUDGET = 16.0
    name = {fm[0]: fm[1] for fm in FMS}
    out = []
    p0 = simulate(set(), {}, N, 1)
    out.append("## Anterior (prior), no pre-work\nP(pass all bars) = %.3f | A fail %.3f | B fail %.3f | KILL fail %.3f" % p0)
    chosen, spent, curve = greedy(BUDGET, {})
    p1 = simulate(chosen, {}, N, 1)
    out.append("\n## Blue team plan (budget %.0f h): mitigations in order of value per hour" % BUDGET)
    for (i, gain, hrs, cum) in curve: out.append("- FM%d %s: +%.3f for %.1f h (cumulative %.3f)" % (i, name[i], gain, hrs, cum))
    out.append("Spent %.1f h. P(pass) = %.3f | A %.3f | B %.3f | KILL %.3f" % ((spent,) + p1))
    out.append("\n## Posterior readiness curve (plan applied, evidence accumulates)")
    mult = {}
    out.append("- start: %.3f" % simulate(chosen, mult, N, 1)[0])
    for ev, eff in EVENTS:
        for k, v in eff.items(): mult[k] = mult.get(k, 1.0) * v
        out.append("- after %s: %.3f" % (ev, simulate(chosen, dict(mult), N, 1)[0]))
    final_mult = dict(mult)
    out.append("\n## Red team: single-FM stress (x1.8) against the blue plan")
    base = simulate(chosen, {}, 20000, 3)[0]; rows = []
    for fm in FMS:
        m = {fm[0]: 1.8}; rows.append((simulate(chosen, m, 20000, 3)[0] - base, fm[0]))
    for d, i in sorted(rows)[:5]: out.append("- FM%d %s: P(pass) %+.3f" % (i, name[i], d))
    worst = None
    for a in range(len(FMS)):
        for b in range(a + 1, len(FMS)):
            m = {FMS[a][0]: 1.8, FMS[b][0]: 1.8}; v = simulate(chosen, m, 5000, 5)[0]
            if worst is None or v < worst[0]: worst = (v, FMS[a][0], FMS[b][0])
    out.append("Worst pair: FM%d + FM%d -> P(pass) %.3f" % (worst[1], worst[2], worst[0]))
    out.append("\n## Inverse reasoning: cheapest path to a target P(pass) (mitigations only, then with evidence events)")
    path_chosen, path_spent, path_curve = greedy(24.0, {}, n=8000, seed=11)
    cum, picked, targets = 0.0, set(), [0.45, 0.55, 0.65]
    hit = {}
    for (i, gain, hrs, _) in path_curve:
        cum += hrs; picked.add(i)
        pv = simulate(picked, {}, 40000, 2)[0]
        for t in targets:
            if t not in hit and pv >= t: hit[t] = (cum, sorted(picked), pv)
    for t in targets:
        if t in hit: out.append("- target %.2f: reached at %.1f h of mitigation (P=%.3f) with FMs %s" % (t, hit[t][0], hit[t][2], hit[t][1]))
        else:
            pe = simulate(path_chosen, dict(final_mult), 40000, 2)[0]
            out.append("- target %.2f: NOT reached by mitigations alone within 24 h (max %.3f); with all evidence events: %.3f" % (t, simulate(path_chosen, {}, 40000, 2)[0], pe))
    out.append("\n## Pathogen and kill-bar view (KILL fail rate by mitigation)")
    out.append("No mitigation %.3f -> plan %.3f -> plan + all evidence events %.3f" % (p0[3], p1[3], simulate(chosen, final_mult, N, 1)[3]))
    print("\n".join(out))

if __name__ == "__main__": main()

SSOT: monday.com take-home prep (single source of truth)

Updated Thu Oct 8 2026. Private. This file is canonical; PREP-BOARD.html is a view of it. Edit this first, then the board. Contains no credentials, no assignment content, no real names of team members.

1. Status

  • Role: Forward Deployed Engineer, Strategic Deployments, monday.com. Hiring-manager call done Oct 8; advanced to the assignment stage.
  • Assignment: invitation received; content (intro video, pre-read, materials, checklist) is behind a one-time secure link that has NOT been opened. Deadline confirmed with Sam: Thursday Oct 15 2026, 5pm ET. Internal target: submit Wed Oct 14 evening.
  • Deliverable format (from the invitation): one ZIP under 10 MB with non-empty source/ and presentation/ folders.
  • Open decision: which browser and device to finish on, and when to open the link (soon, so there is time to ask follow-ups).

2. Files and what each is for

FilePurpose
ATLAS.html (built by atlas/build_atlas.py)One-file Atlas of every prep document as a ziggurat (base: witnessed signal; apex: decision), with gates re-run on every build; atlas/atlas-data.json is the data object for HUD visualizers

3. Decisions made

  1. Do not open the link until the browser and device are chosen; no incognito, no cookie clearing, no forwarding; the link is a credential and is stored nowhere.
  2. Pre-work is scaffolding, not pre-solving: log, rubric, deliverable skeleton, sandbox practice, rehearsal plan.
  3. The deliverable is yours: every AI use logged and disclosed; every file explainable.
  4. Respectful framing of monday's own projects: say what an eval needs next, never what is broken; no third-party names; counts re-pulled the same day.
  5. ARCS is shown as a discipline built on honest evidence, not as a proven or certified system; keep private IP out of the ZIP unless deliberately released.
  6. Only offer to compound one or two reusable assets, chosen after reading the brief.

4. Research findings (static reads; nothing was run)

  • monday's own pages say little about this loop. The engineering interview guide dates from 2020 and covers software-engineering roles; the careers page says four to five weeks; the AI interview guide is the only current policy (disclose, own, explain).
  • Adjacent customer-facing take-homes (Glassdoor, anecdotal): build a workflow in monday for a client scenario, present it, then defend it and sometimes extend it live; one candidate was told they "didn't build a deck." No report on this exact track.
  • Open source (mondaycom): active MCP server and agent toolkit with a hosted MCP; sensei (agent qualification engine); agent-tool-protocol; agentic-monday (a Claude Code plugin marketplace); vibe design system; apps SDK and CLI. No official Hugging Face organization found.
  • Sensei read in source: clean suite schema and scoring math; but the judge never sees fixtures, two of four adapters drop fixtures, the agent model name is fixed, judge controls are minimal, layers 2 and 3 are weak, and shipped suites are thin. Looks dormant since March 2026. These are source reads, not reproduced.
  • Platform facts: MCP calls count against the daily API budget; MCP actions run under the user's permissions; no self-service per-tool-call audit export; read-only is a tool-registration filter; hosted MCP source is not public.
  • Team (roles only): the deployment function looks formed from Professional Services and implementation, with two deeply technical voices. Titles in the deployment family date from Sept and Oct 2026. One strategist describes partnering with Sales on scoping, estimates and SOWs, which supports the before, during and after the sale hypothesis.

5. Risk model (Monte Carlo, subjective priors)

  • No pre-work: P(pass all bars) about 0.24; the KILL bar drives about 0.37 of failures.
  • With about 15.5 hours of mitigations: about 0.52; with evidence events (brief read, rehearsal, dry run, gates, independent clear): about 0.65.
  • Biggest value per hour: log every repair (0.5 h), confidentiality rule (0.5 h), link dry run (1.5 h), claim and consistency gates (2 h), outcome framing (2 h), acceptance criteria (3 h), rehearsal (4 h).
  • Red team: platform fluency gap is the weakest point; worst pair is "engineering demo, not outcome" plus platform fluency.
  • Not yet modeled: failure modes 14 to 17 (criticizing monday's own repo, unrun claims stated as fact, stale counts, heavy ARCS vocabulary).

6. Runway

Oct 8: prep, confirm deadline. Oct 9: activate, watch the video, read the pre-read, reconcile the rubric, write acceptance criteria and a not-doing list. Oct 10 to 12: build in thin slices, log as you go. Oct 13: draft the deck, run mechanical gates. Oct 14: red and blue round, rehearse aloud, package, submit in the evening. Oct 15: buffer; deadline 5pm ET.

No monday code was run. Personas are hypotheses. Subjective priors are not predictions. The leave-behind one-sheet still needs the gauntlet fixes. No unrun defect claim about any third-party system should be stated as fact.
